thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: GPU allocation backlog in us-west-2-gpu-pool > 95%. queue_length=1400, pending_requests=1180. autoscaler reported: scale_limit_reached & throttle_backoff. Several MIG flavors report stranded slices. Possible customer impact on hosted API (text generation)

alex: ack. oncall maya? i'm dropping in to coordinate until we have a primary.

maya: i'm oncall, taking this. thanks alex. quick status—any errors from the allocator?

zhen: I pulled the allocator logs. high-level: a burst of requests ~10:10 triggered replicas to request new allocations but the autoscaler hit a global scale cap (we have a 120 node soft-limit). The allocator kept queueing requests; placement failed due to MIG binpack fragmentation (lots of leftover 1g slices and few 4g/8g). Many pods pending with reason "Insufficient GPUs".

zhen: snippet from allocator: 
```
ERROR allocator: placement failed: insufficient resources for workload redwood-35b-q4_0 replica=12
reason: compatible_mig_slice_not_found
```

emily_custsuccess: Customer impact: SLO alerts for 5 customers in last 10m. Reports: sustained 5xx rate increase and generation latency > 5s for queued requests. Not yet a broader outage but CS is seeing multiple escalations.

maya: OK. immediate mitigation options: 1) evict non-critical workloads from dedicated pools we control and shift capacity; 2) force-repack MIG slices to larger sizes (risky); 3) fall back traffic to smaller model variant (redwood-13b) until we stabilize. Which do we want to try first?

ops_lead: We should avoid risky live MIG resize unless we have explicit runbook. Prioritize draining low-priority jobs and routing traffic to region fallback (us-east). Also, can we temporarily lift the soft scale cap? That will let autoscaler request new nodes if cloud quota allows.

zhen: checking quotas now. Cloud project quota for GPU nodes currently at 130; soft cap at 120. If we bump the soft cap to 128 we might relieve pressure quickly. However, fragmentation will still leave some slots unusable for 35b instances. Pack efficiency currently ~61%.

maya: actioning steps: (1) increase autoscaler soft_limit to 128 — emily, can you coordinate with infra to confirm we can spin nodes? (2) drain non-prod pools: mark pool "batch-inference" as low-priority and evict. (3) initiate traffic steering policy to route 20% of traffic to redwood-13b across hosted for the next 15m.

emily_custsuccess: on it, pinged infra and marketplace quota owners. also notifying affected customers with a short status note: "We are mitigating increased latency by balancing capacity and routing to fallback models; no data loss."

zhen: meanwhile I'm prepping a manual packing job to rebalance existing MIG slices. plan: create new nodes with 8g slices, launch an empty daemontset to attract small slices, then drain+repack older nodes to consolidate. This is disruptive but less risky than in-place resizing.

alex: do we have a runbook for manual repack? last time it was tedious. we need step-by-step and a safe rollback.

zhen: minimal steps I'm going to execute (will post commands as I run them):
1) terraform apply pool expansion (soft cap bump)
2) scale down batch-inference: kubectl -n batch set replicas deployment/batch-workers 0 --record
3) create temporary packing job: ./tools/pack-run --target-pool us-west-2-gpu-pool --prefer-mig=8g --dry-run=false
4) drain nodes with cordon+drain and wait for critical pods to reschedule.

maya: i'll coordinate safety: hold on 'pack-run' until we've confirmed eviction of low-priority jobs and infra confirms node spin-up. also, enable autoscaler verbose debug so we can monitor any further throttle.

pagerbot: Deploy bot: terraform apply started by zhen. Plan: +6 nodes in us-west-2-gpu-pool. (link: https://ci.internal/plan/4573)

ops_lead: good. also open a temporary rate-limit on per-tenant tokens to avoid single-customer storms worsening packing. set token_concurrency=5 for free-tier and 10 for paid for next 30m.

emily_custsuccess: CS update posted to customers affected. infra responded: quota allow spin-up to 130 nodes, but provisioning will take ~4-6 minutes per node.

zhen: starting pack-run now (after low-priority evictions). logs: "packing: migrated 18 small slices into 4 new 8g nodes; freed 22 older nodes for consolidation". queue_length dropping from 1400 -> 620 over 5m. pending_requests now 540.

maya: nice. keep an eye on model-specific queue (35b) — it's still at ~220 pending. if it doesn't drop below 100 in 10m, we switch more traffic to 13b.

alex: customer impact watch: 5xx rate dropped by 40% after routing and packing. still some throttled requests though. good progress.

ops_lead: next steps (short term): (a) finish repack, (b) temporarily raise soft cap to 130 if packing stalls, (c) create incident postmortem ticket with action items: improve autoscaler packing heuristics, add emergency repack runbook, tighten per-tenant surge controls.

jordan: i'm next oncall in 40m. maya — do you want to hand off once things are stable?

maya: i'll keep it until we reach queue_length < 200 and 35b pending < 50. if we hit that in 20m i'll hand off to you. otherwise i'll update in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident note added: priority=P1, classification=gpu_capacity_exhaustion, started_at=4071234567. Postmortem owner assigned: ops_lead.

maya: thanks all — tidy up logs, attach packing logs and autoscaler debug output to the incident ticket. we'll run a follow-up tomorrow to tune packer heuristics and consider making repack tooling less manual. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: Deploy bot: terraform apply completed. 6 nodes added to us-west-2-gpu-pool.

zhen: final status update: queue_length=160, pending_requests=139, 35b pending=42. packing efficiency up to 81%. no new customer escalations in last 10m. marking mitigation phase as complete.

maya: handing off to jordan now. jordan — full notes are in the incident ticket. If anything regresses, @jordan please escalate to ops_lead immediately.

jordan: thanks maya, taking over. reviewing notes now. good work team.

incident-bot: Incident resolved to mitigation state at 4071235789. Please continue monitoring and add any follow-up tasks to the postmortem."
